problem_type: Directory fsync barrier copied per module with divergent platform handling
symptom: On Windows, creating or opening any project fails in the main process and the renderer only sees project_agent_unavailable; the project library never navigates into the project. The Electron director walkthrough could not open a project at all.
direct_cause: projectAgentMigration.archiveLegacySources and projectAgentRepository.fsyncDirectory open a directory fd and call fsyncSync on it; Windows opens directory handles fine but FlushFileBuffers on a directory handle raises EPERM, which the IPC envelope masks as project_agent_unavailable.
class_root: The 'open a directory fd only to fsync it' barrier had no shared owner: eight modules each carried their own copy, and each copy decided differently whether unsupported-platform errors are swallowed (catch-all, win32 early return, openSync-only guard, or no guard).
affected_population: Every Windows user opening or creating a project (project agent host initialize / legacy archive)
Every durable directory barrier in the main process: lease store, production-run lock and intent log, workspace manifest lock, cutover manifest, proposal receipt store, certification persistence
entry_points: nomi:projectAgent:open IPC (project agent host initialize + legacy migration)
production run lock and intent log append

external_sources.purpose: fs.fsyncSync contract; Windows directory handles cannot be flushed, the failure surfaces as EPERM
uv__fs_fsync on win32 calls FlushFileBuffers; directory handles opened for read fail with access denied → EPERM

invariants: There is exactly one implementation of the directory barrier, electron/durability.fsyncDirectoryIfDurable.

In durable mode the barrier opens the directory and fsyncs it; platform codes that mean 'no directory fsync available' (EPERM, EACCES, EINVAL, ENOTSUP, EISDIR, EBADF) return silently, every other error propagates.
In ephemeral mode the barrier does not open the directory at all.
No module outside durability.ts opens a directory fd for the purpose of fsync.
generality_proof: grep for fsyncDirectory / fsyncNomiDirectory / fsyncReceiptDirectory / 'openSync(dir, "r")' + fsyncIfDurable across electron/ found eight copies; all eight now delegate to fsyncDirectoryIfDurable, and the heavy-path gate's unguarded-fsync rule already forbids raw fs.fsyncSync outside durability.ts, so a new copy cannot reintroduce a raw fsync. The remaining way to regress is a new module re-implementing open+fsyncIfDurable on a directory fd; the class regression test pins that only durability.ts contains that shape.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the durable directory barrier including the platform-unsupported error set; callers pass a directory path and never touch the fd.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: ensurePartitionDirectory / fsyncPublishedMain / command ledger fsyncDirectory dep
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Local fsyncDirectory removed; all call sites and the ledger dependency use fsyncDirectoryIfDurable.
Local fsyncDirectory (open + fsyncIfDurable, no platform guard) removed; this was the copy that broke Windows project open.
Thin wrapper now delegates; the win32 early return moved into the shared barrier.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: lease publish / issue / prune directory barriers
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Local catch-all copy removed; five call sites delegate.
Wrapper keeps the dirname convenience and delegates.
Inline open + fsyncSync block replaced by the shared call.
Local catch-all copy removed; nine call sites delegate.
Inline isDurable + open + fsyncIfDurable block replaced by the shared call.
Only fsyncs the temp file fd through fsyncIfDurable; it never opens a directory fd.

recurrence.reason: The same barrier was re-implemented eight times with four different Windows policies; every new durable write path is a place where the ninth copy would appear.
same_class_scan: grep -rn 'function fsync' electron --include=*.ts (excluding tests) → 8 local copies, all migrated.
grep -rln fsyncIfDurable electron | xargs grep -l 'O_RDONLY\|, "r")' → certificationPersistence, projectAgentCommandLedger (file fd only, not affected), projectAgentProposalReceiptStore.
check:heavy-path unguarded-fsync = 0 after the change (raw fsyncSync only inside durability.ts).

prevention.invariant: Directory barriers go through fsyncDirectoryIfDurable; platform-unsupported errors are classified once.
prevention.failure_mode: A module that re-implements the barrier is caught by the class regression test in electron/durability.test.ts (only durability.ts may pair a read-only directory openSync with fsync); a raw fsyncSync is caught by the pre-existing check:heavy-path unguarded-fsync rule.
prevention.strategy: Add the shared helper next to fsyncIfDurable, delete every local copy in the same change, and pin the single-implementation invariant with a source scan test.

legacy_paths.rationale: The per-module fsyncDirectory / fsyncNomiDirectory / inline directory-fsync copies in these files are deleted in the same change; two thin wrappers (productionRunLock.fsyncDirectory, proposalReceiptStore.fsyncReceiptDirectory) only compute the directory path and delegate.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The behaviour is Node's fs semantics on Windows; no dependency version controls it.

migration: No persisted data changes. Existing project folders that failed to open on Windows open on the next launch; nothing was written in the failed attempts beyond the legacy archive directory, which the migration re-validates by hash.
residual_risks: On filesystems that reject directory fsync the barrier degrades to file-only durability; this matches the previous catch-all copies and is documented in durability.ts.
Windows symlink-privilege and 1,000-command timeout failures in the same electron test files are environment-specific on this machine and unrelated to the barrier.
